newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police shoot Palestinian at roadblock.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police shoot Palestinian at roadblock.

text.p: Police shot and wounded a Palestinian who refused an order to stop at a roadblock that had been set up in central Israel on Thursday for fear of a guerrilla attack, army radio said.
It said police first fired in the air to stop a van from running a roadblock near Tel Aviv. The man got out and fled towards a field. Police shot him when he refused an order to stop.
Four or five other Palestinians in the car were arrested. The radio said they had forged identity cards.
The man was seriously wounded and not killed, as reported earlier, the radio said. Police found the car was not booby-trapped.
Israel set up roadblocks to enforce a closure imposed overnight on the West Bank and Gaza Strip for fear of a guerrilla attack.

Officials said the Jewish state had gone on high security alert ahead of the anniversary of the assassination of Fathi Shqaqi, the leader of the militant Islamic Jihad group behind suicide attacks in Israel.
Shqaqi was gunned down in Malta on October 26 last year in what Palestinians believe was an attack by Israel's Mossad secret service. The militant group has vowed to avenge his murder.
Israelis were also remembering the assassination of prime minister Yitzhak Rabin on the first anniversary of his death according to the Jewish calendar.
